newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinans say Israelis return two abducted boys.
newsitem.headline: Palestinans say Israelis return two abducted boys.

text.p: Israeli undercover soldiers abducted and briefly held two Palestinian boys from the West Bank village of Husan, where a Jewish settler allegedly killed a boy a week ago, Palestinians said on Monday.
They said Mazen Shousha, 14, and Alaa al-Oul, 14, were kidnapped near their homes on Sunday.
"The two boys were kidnapped by Israeli undercover units driving a Ford car with Palestinian number plates," said a member of one of the boys' families, who spoke on condition he not be identified.

"The Palestinian Liaison Committee was informed of the abduction, and after lengthy talks with the Israeli Liaison Committee, the two boys were returned at one a.m. on Monday (2300 GMT on Sunday)," he said.
Husan is in an area of the West Bank that, in interim peace deals between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO), falls under both Israeli and PLO authorities.

The Israeli army said in reaction: "An army force operating in Husan at night stopped two stone throwers. The two were taken by Israeli police for questioning and were released on bail to their parents."
On Sunday, a Jerusalem court ordered Jewish settler Nahum Kurman held until the end of criminal proceedings against him in the case of the dead boy, Hilmi Shousha, 11. Mazen Shousha is a relative.
Israeli authorities on Friday charged Kurman, security chief of the Jewish settlement of Hadar Beitar, with manslaughter.
They said he kicked Hilmi Shousha to the ground, placed his foot on the boy's neck and beat him on the head with a pistol butt while on a hunt for stone throwers a week ago.
